title: Hierarchical Context Pruning: Optimizing Real-World Code Completion with Repository-Level Pretrained Code LLMs
budget_tradeoff_detail: HCP compresses full-repository context from 50,000+ tokens to ~8,000 tokens while improving EM by roughly 3-6 points across six Code LLMs (DeepseekCoder, Starcoder2, CodeGemma variants).
confound_note: Headline comparison (Random-All baseline vs HCP) varies both representation (flat concatenation vs hierarchical dependency-graph+embedding pruning) and token budget (~50k vs ~8k) simultaneously; secondary ablations (Table 2 dependency-level D1..Dinf, Table 3 pruning-level P0-P2) hold the max context window fixed while varying representation/pruning depth, giving a budget-matched comparison for those specific tables.

budget_tradeoff_detail: WebDesignIter achieves higher Pass@1 (33.53% vs 21.27%) than Claude Code while using ~26x fewer input tokens (533K vs 13,949K) (Table 4, RQ4) - its structured KG retrieval is both cheaper and more accurate than general-purpose agentic exploration.

title: Beyond "What to Retrieve": Uncertainty in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
budget_tradeoff_detail: OpenCoder matches baseline RAG's five-candidate generation budget and at-most-two repair rounds exactly, isolating uncertainty-aware filtering/ranking as the sole varied factor; the +21.88pp gain (GPT, selected-output correctness) is attributable to the mechanism, not extra budget — though OpenCoder ties RAG+Verify/Repair at 78.13%, so the advantage vanishes once verification/repair is added (RQ3)
confound_note: RQ3's three arms (Baseline RAG, RAG+Verify/Repair, OpenCoder) hold retrieval evidence and candidate/repair budgets constant, varying only whether uncertainty-aware filtering/ranking/repair is applied — a genuine budget-matched comparison; however the Gemini backend shows no statistically supported gain, indicating the effect is backend-dependent

title: Paritok-4B: Intent-Conditioned Context Compression for Coding Agents

key_numbers.metric: compression ratio vs quality retained (Paritok-4B, line-numbered input)

key_numbers.value: 96.0% (96.2% held-out) of emitted tokens present in input

budget_tradeoff_detail: Paritok-4B compresses trajectories to 25.7-27.8% of original size while retaining 86.5-89.3% of uncompressed single-shot SWE-bench Lite solve quality, compressing 2.0-2.4x harder than GPT-5/GPT-4.1-mini compressors; self-hosted compressor breaks even vs. sending uncompressed context when hosting cost is below $2.23/million tokens.
confound_note: Compares Paritok-4B against GPT-5 and GPT-4.1-mini used as ad hoc compressors on the same trajectories/downstream agent (Claude Sonnet); compression ratios are NOT held constant across the three compressors (25.7% vs 50.2% vs 61.9%), so quality-retention differences are confounded with how aggressively each compressor happens to compress.
